steps.say: This lesson shows **Facet**, the language the AI writes every desktop in, and how a design file becomes what is on the screen. A Facet document is markup for structure and a small stylesheet for looks, like HTML and CSS but much smaller and made for this OS.
The engine is in userland/shell/fm: xml.c reads the markup, css.c the styles, layout.c places things, render.c draws them, doc.c handles input, lint.c spots mistakes.

steps.through: * to write, easy to validate, and easy for the companion to read and drive.
steps.say: Nothing about the layout is built in. A taskbar with a start menu and a dock with a menu bar are just two different documents.

steps.anchor: /* A lenient XML subset parser. Models write markup well but not perfectly,
steps.say: Models make small mistakes, so the reader mends what it can, such as unclosed tags or bare ampersands, and notes each problem rather than refusing the document.
Text becomes a document tree with `fm_parse`, and goes back to text with `fm_serialize`. That is how the design is saved.
Each frame the desktop calls `fm_layout` to place everything at the screen's size, then `fm_render_layer` to draw it into the frame.
The 34 starter themes are Facet documents too. Reading one is the quickest way to learn the language.
`<style>` starts with variables for colours, fonts and corners. Every theme uses the same names, so changing them recolours the whole desktop.
`<desktop>` is the structure: columns, clocks, app lists, buttons and popovers. A button's `what` is its action, such as `toggle:#all`, from a fixed set.
`<template id="window">` is the frame drawn around every window, apps' windows included. `<slot/>` is where the window's content goes.
The design in use is kept in /etc/os/facet.xml and read at start (main.c). `desktop_enter` puts it on screen, and makes one from the older design settings if there is no document.
Every change is saved back to that file. The version before is kept as a change that can be put back (lesson 10).
The AI may start from a theme, `<facet base="paper">`, and write only what changes. Its style rules go after the theme's, and later rules win.
One thing to know: the list of themes offered to the AI stops at 24 names, but there are 34 theme files. The rest are not offered here.
Apps the companion writes use **Facet 2**, a separate app language (.facet files, docs/facet2.md, userland/shell/fx). Next: **08 The companion**.
